entries.title: Evaluator selections are kept when searching or changing plan filters
entries.summary: Checking an evaluator, then searching for another one, used to clear every earlier pick. Selections now survive a new search or plan-filter change; only switching events resets them. When some selected evaluators are not visible in the current search results, the selection bar shows **N not in this list** so the count is always clear before a bulk tag action.
entries.use_case: Events with hundreds of evaluators often need to find and tag several people across multiple searches. Organizers can now check evaluators one search at a time and bulk-apply tags to all of them in a single action without losing earlier picks.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer with a large evaluator pool (100+) reports that bulk-tagging evaluators is tedious because selections disappear between searches.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Sessions 2.0 evaluation plans with many evaluators who need to bulk-apply tags across multiple searches.
internal.staff_path: Event → Sessions → Evaluation Plans → [plan] → Evaluators tab
internal.gotchas: The selection bar shows 'N not in this list' when selected evaluators are off the current page — reassure customers this is expected and those people are still included in the bulk request. Only switching events clears the selection; searching and plan-filter changes do not.
internal.talk_track: You can now search for evaluators one group at a time, check each one, and when you hit Edit Tags all your picks across every search are included — no need to tag them in separate passes.

draft.docs_gap: The Manage evaluators section should note that selections persist across searches and plan-filter changes, and explain the "N not in this list" indicator in the selection bar.

entries.title: Bulk edit participant order across sessions
entries.summary: In **As submitted** mode, a new **Bulk edit order** page (from the **⋯** menu on a session's Participants list, or **More → Order participants** on selected sessions) sets one ordering rule — roles in the order you choose, then last name, first name, affiliation and more — previews which sessions would change, and reorders them all at once. Participants added later keep their submitted order until you apply the rules again.

enable.path: Program → Settings → Roles → Participant display order: As submitted

where.path: Session → Participants → ⋯ → Bulk edit order; Sessions → select → More → Order participants

entries.use_case: Programs that show participants as one list often still want a house style — moderators first, then speakers alphabetically. Instead of dragging each session by hand, organizers set the rule once and apply it to every session or a selection, with a preview first.

cs_action.note: Available wherever Participant Ordering Controls is on and the event uses As submitted.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer in As submitted mode asks to put moderators or chairs first, or to alphabetize speakers, across many sessions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events already on Participant Ordering Controls with As submitted display order — typically medical/scientific programs and panels-heavy conferences.
internal.staff_path: Event → Sessions → [session] → Participants → ⋯ → Bulk edit order
internal.gotchas: Applying is a one-time reorder, not a live sort: new participants land in submitted order until the rules are applied again. Not available in By role mode. Sessions already in order are skipped and not marked as updated.
internal.talk_track: Set the order once — roles in the order you want, then by last name — preview which sessions change, and reorder them all in one click.
